# Worked example — generated by the agent

One run of `agent/agent.py` against `../../reference/case/s25UltraTHIKnoCutout.3mf`.
Everything here was produced by the tool; nothing is hand-modelled.

The two printable parts from this run also ship in the Human Kit's
`Examples/` folder (`perimeter_TPU.stl`, `backplate_rigid.stl`), because that
package is a standalone download and has to work on its own. `--mirror
../Human_Kit/Examples` writes them there; run it after any change so the two
never drift. Everything else in this folder — the normalised case, the cutter
and the reports — exists for the agent workflow and stays here.

```sh
cd Agent_Pack
python3 agent/agent.py --case reference/case/s25UltraTHIKnoCutout.3mf \
                       --out examples/s25-ultra-thik
```

| file | what it is | print? |
|---|---|---|
| `01_case_normalised.stl` | the input, repaired, back face at Z=0 | no — input |
| `02_cutter.stl` | the Human Kit cutter at the fitted parameters | no — tool |
| `04_perimeter.stl` | TPU perimeter, 83.15 × 167.60 × 11.93 mm | yes, TPU |
| `05_backplate.stl` | rigid backplate with tracks, springs and window cut in | yes, rigid |
| `06_housing_negative.stl` | the housing negative on its own | no — tool |
| `report.md`, `report.json` | every number measured and assumed | — |

## What the run found

- back face at z = −2.80 mm, panel 2.80 mm thick
- visible outline 78.89 × 164.09 mm, **fitted** to 77.89 × 163.09 mm
- split into exactly 2 parts: 13914 mm³ + 27654 mm³ = the input's 41573 mm³
- housing 33.2 × 145.7 mm, **8720 mm³** removed, backplate still one part

The fitted outline is 1 mm smaller than the measured one because the case walls
are 12 mm tall at the edge; a ring cut there leaves material above the cutter and
the halves never separate.

## Placement

The back panel has one through-opening:

| | |
|---|---|
| opening 0 | x 4.78…36.78, y 3.78…60.78 — **32.0 × 57.0 mm**, the camera cluster |
| camera end | low Y, so the springs face the top and the housing is **rotated 180°** |
| housing rect | x 38.92…72.12, y 8.55…154.25 |
| clear zone | backplate inset 5.2 mm (3.2 interlock band + 2.0 margin) |
| clearance to opening | **2.14 mm** |

Two things drove this result, and both were wrong in the first attempt:

**Never centre.** A centred housing runs straight through the camera opening.
The strap housing is a negative volume, so the result is a backplate whose strap
window has merged into the camera hole: it slices, it looks fine in the viewport,
and it cannot be assembled.

**The interlock is not free space.** The outer 3.2 mm of a split backplate is the
TPU tongue's retaining rail. With only a 2 mm edge margin the spring relief
pockets reached into that band on one side, and sat 1.5 mm from the camera
opening on the other. The clear zone is now the backplate inset by
`joint_inset + margin` = 5.2 mm.

## Why the strap is the width it is

With the original 19.60 mm band and 7.10 mm ears the housing was 37.0 mm wide and
the layout above was impossible: one spring relief pocket reached into the
interlock band, the other sat 1.5 mm from the camera. At the 2.0 mm rule the tool
refused, reporting 36.5 mm as the widest housing that would fit.

The band was narrowed to 16.60 mm. The ears then have two opposing constraints:

- **too wide** and the housing cannot fit — the spring pockets sit at
  `track_outer + body + relief`, so every millimetre of ear becomes a millimetre
  of housing width;
- **too narrow** and the strap pulls out of the track under load, which is a
  dropped phone.

The working figure is **6.40 mm ears**, which is the widest that keeps the
0.80 mm lateral clearance they need while the 33.2 mm housing still clears the
camera by 2.14 mm and the interlock band by 2.42 mm. That is below the original
7.10 mm — the version that was actually tested in a case — so it stays inside
known-good territory.

Ear centres move with the band: 25.50 → 21.80 mm, tracks 26.00 → 22.60 mm at
7.20 mm wide. A 6.40 mm ear needs its inner edge inside the 8.30 mm band
half-width, so the centre spacing is capped at ~22.0 mm regardless.

The 0.80 mm clearance is two 0.40 mm extrusion widths. Below one line width a
slicer fills the gap with a sliver; two lines is reliably a void. It widens the
track, which shortens the detent engagement, so `strap_detent_nose_depth` went
1.25 → 1.55 mm to hold engagement at the previously validated 0.75 mm.

## Strap fit

The strap sits with its underside on the track floor: **+0.60 mm** in Z. Placed
at Z=0 its ears sink into the floor (94 mm³ of interference); at +0.60 mm the
intersection with the backplate is **0.00 mm³**.
